claims.text: CoCrFeNiMo0.85 can be prepared as an adherent high-entropy-alloy coating.
The CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coating is suitable for application to aerospace fasteners.
Optimized laser shock peening will create a deep gradient-nanostructured surface layer with compressive residual stress.
Optimizing LSP pulse energy, overlap, and pulse parameters can extend the modified layer deeply enough to influence near-surface bulk properties.
Carefully calibrated LSP parameters can avoid surface cracking and produce a uniform residual-stress distribution.
A controlled processing atmosphere will prevent oxidation during LSP.
The treated layer will have refined grains and high compressive residual stress.
Compressive residual stress and surface grain refinement hinder crack initiation and thereby improve fatigue resistance and mechanical durability.
The refined nanostructure hinders dislocation movement.
A sufficiently deep LSP-modified layer acts as a barrier to room-temperature dislocation creep.
LSP promotes formation of a more stable and dense passive oxide film on CoCrFeNiMo0.85.
LSP-treated CoCrFeNiMo0.85 will have significantly longer fatigue life than the untreated material.
LSP-treated CoCrFeNiMo0.85 will have a lower room-temperature creep strain rate than the untreated material.
LSP-treated CoCrFeNiMo0.85 will exhibit lower corrosion current density and improved passivation relative to the untreated material.
Untreated CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coatings can provide corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature.
The combined improvements should persist under room-temperature mechanical loading and salt-spray-like corrosive exposure.
The benefits will diminish if the modified layer is too shallow or if loading extends beyond the region influenced by that layer.
